title: PRD: Dedicated safety-net headroom contracts and eviction hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This PRD defines a lightweight "safety‑net headroom" contract for Dedicated capacity customers and an associated set of configurable eviction hooks. The goal is to give tenants predictable, contract-backed short‑term headroom during transient bursts while providing deterministic eviction machinery and observability so product, infra, and SRE teams can protect latency SLAs and meet fairness guarantees.

Problem statement / Background:
Dedicated pools give tenants reserved capacity, but we observe two common failure modes in production: (1) short-lived burst traffic that exceeds committed capacity and forces manual interventions or noisy autoscale spikes, and (2) heavy-tailed incidents where aggressive preemption or coarse eviction causes wide SLA regressions for lower-priority tenants. Existing reserved/burst logic lacks a standard contract that balances short-term elasticity with predictable eviction behavior.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Provide a documented contract for short-duration headroom allocation that tenants can opt into (duration, magnitude, and billing implications).
- Implement eviction hooks that allow tenants to declare graceful degradation boundaries (e.g., degrade to smaller batch sizes, enable a latency-first fallback model, or temporarily reduce quality knobs) prior to hard preemption.
- Ensure platform operators can enforce fairness and predictable tail-latency during multi-tenant contention while keeping customer-visible outages to a minimum.
- Full observability and alerting for headroom consumption, eviction events, and rollback actions.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for long-term autoscale/reservation changes (this is for transient bursts only).
- Not proposing new pricing tiers today; billing model will be metered and communicated outside this sprint.

User personas:
- Platform product manager (configures headroom templates and policies).
- Tenant owner/engineer (opts into headroom and configures eviction hooks for their workload).
- SRE/operator (monitors headroom use, enforces caps, and runs rollback).

User stories:
- As a tenant owner, I want up to 30 seconds of 2x headroom per tenant once per 10 minutes so short bursts finish without manual escalation.
- As a platform PM, I want a flag to require tenants to define an eviction hook (graceful fallback behavior) before enabling headroom on a pool.
- As an SRE, I want to audit who consumed headroom, the exact fallback sequence invoked, and observed latency impact within 5 minutes of the event.

Key requirements (functional):
1) Headroom contract:
   - Policy parameters: max_multiplier (1.1–3.0), max_duration_seconds (<= 300), cooldown_seconds (>= 60), per-tenant monthly headroom budget (optional).
   - Activation modes: explicit tenant request (API/Console), automatic on burst if tenant has opt-in flag.
   - Metering: token-level metering during headroom windows for billing and usage quotas.

2) Eviction hooks API:
   - Tenants must provide a single "eviction_hook" descriptor when enabling headroom. The descriptor is an opaque string pointing to a canonical fallback plan (examples: "degrade-q3", "reduce-batch-2x", "fallback-to-cpu-model").
   - Platform exposes predefined hook templates; tenants may request custom hooks subject to review.

3) Deterministic eviction pipeline:
   - When capacity pressure crosses configured threshold, system invokes eviction hooks in order: notify tenant -> apply soft-degradation (hook) -> wait grace_period -> hard eviction if still over threshold.
   - Grace periods must be configurable per pool; default 30s.

4) Observability and auditing:
   - Events: headroom_requested, headroom_granted, hook_invoked, degrade_applied, hard_eviction, headroom_expired.
   - Dashboards: per-tenant headroom consumption, average latency delta during headroom windows, eviction frequency.

5) Policy enforcement and fairness:
   - Global tenant fairshare enforced via proportional reduction if multiple tenants simultaneously request headroom beyond pool capacity.
   - Operator override allowlist for emergency reclaim.

Constraints and non-functional requirements:
- Latency SLOs: the headroom and eviction process must not add >10ms p50 overhead to normal requests when idle.
- Rollout safety: feature behind gated flag for dedicated clusters; default off for new tenants.
- Scale: must support 5k concurrent headroom grants per region.

API / Console changes:
- Add POST /v1/dedicated/headroom-requests to request headroom with payload {tenant_id, multiplier, duration, eviction_hook}.
- Console UI: new "Headroom" tab in pool settings with toggle, template selector, and per-tenant usage table.

Telemetry and metrics (required):
- Counters: headroom_granted_total, headroom_denied_total, hook_invoked_total, hard_evictions_total.
- Histograms: headroom_duration_seconds, latency_delta_during_headroom_ms.
- Traces: sampled traces linking request set -> hook invocation -> outcome.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
1) End-to-end: A tenant can request a 2x headroom for 60s via API and observe headroom_granted event and increased capacity in real cluster test for that tenant only.
2) Eviction hook flow: When simulated contention exceeds pool capacity, system invokes hook_invoked and applies soft-degradation; if pressure persists beyond grace_period, hard_eviction is emitted and capacity reclaimed.
3) Fairness: With 3 tenants requesting 3x headroom concurrently exceeding pool headroom, system proportionally splits available headroom and logs proportional allocation decisions.
4) Observability: Dashboards show headroom usage and a synthetic test run surfaces correct latency_delta metrics for the window.
5) No regression: Baseline latency overhead for non-headroom traffic is within 10ms p50 of pre-change baseline in controlled benchmark.

Rollout plan / Phases:
- Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): implement API + minimal grant logic + hook invocation in canary clusters behind feature flag. Allow 10 internal tenants.
- Phase 2 (pilot, 6 weeks): open to select customers, full telemetry, console UI in read-only mode.
- Phase 3 (GA): enable console controls, billing metering, and operator overrides.

Migration and backward compatibility:
- Existing tenants that previously relied on opaque burst behavior will not be impacted until they opt-in.
- Default behavior remains unchanged; headroom gating ensures operators don't accidentally enable global burst.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Billing model: per-token premium during headroom vs explicit per-minute headroom credit. Decide by EOW Mar 26.
- Hook expressiveness vs safety: how much control to give tenants to run custom scripts vs choosing templates. Prefer template-first approach.
- Preemption aggressiveness: whether to bias evictions toward opportunistic workloads or strict FIFO. Recommendation: opportunistic first.

Docs and artifacts linked:
- Design notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/headroom-design (draft)
- Mockups (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/specs/headroom-ui-v1
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8242 (canary logic)
- Acceptance test harness: https://qa.redwood.ai/headroom-sim

Operational playbook (short):
- On headroom alert, SRE checks headroom_granted_total and hook_invoked_total; if repeated hard_evictions occur >3x in 1h, escalate to capacity engineering and contact tenant owners.
- Postmortem checklist includes: timeline of headroom events, hook behaviors, and any billing disputes.

Owners and stakeholders:
- Product owner: Aisha Patel
- Engineering lead: Miguel Santos
- SRE: Lara Nguyen
- Security/compliance reviewer: Priya Kapoor

Next steps (this cycle):
- Finalize API schema and minimal eviction hook templates (owner: Miguel) by 2026-03-18.
- Implement canary grant logic and event emission (owner: ENG-48923) by 2026-04-05.
- Prepare pilot tenant list and communications (owner: Aisha) by 2026-04-12.

Acceptance test checklist (QA):
- Unit tests for policy enforcement and cooldowns.
- Integration test that simulates capacity pressure and verifies hook ordering and metrics.
- Performance regression test to assert <10ms p50 added latency.

This PRD intentionally targets a focused feature set so we can iterate quickly, gather real usage signals, and expand to richer billing and custom hooks in subsequent releases.
